_meta.purpose: PUBLIC dictionary for recognising lab markers in the text of a report (per-language name substrings → the labs.json key, units, references). Feeds the auto-ingest of a folder of lab PDFs. Holds no patient data, portable.
_meta.note:
labels.<lang> holds everything that is a language: names — lower-case substrings to look for in a row of the form; exclude — if one occurs, the row is skipped; require / next_require / form_require and their negatives — the same, scoped to the segment after the name, to the next row, and to the form as a whole; display — the name shown on screen. A language absent from a marker falls back to one that is present.
Language-independent, and deliberately outside labels: unit (a UCUM code — the label for it comes from knowledge/units.json in the output language), units ({unit surface form: multiplier to the canonical unit} — at once a gate and a conversion, populated only where a conversion is genuinely needed), specimen (blood/serum/plasma/urine/stool/saliva), the reference bounds, direction, plausible, loinc.

_meta.key_rule: the marker key is the primary key of a person's series and never changes: a rename would split a series in two. A key that has to be replaced gets an `aliases` entry instead.
_meta.ref_sex: Whose corridor a marker with ONE reference interval holds: `any` (adult interval independent of sex — a class fact for amino and organic acids, stool, flora, autoantibodies, elements, electrolytes, coagulation, blood-count indices, lipids, glucose, vitamins, thyroid, proteins), `male` or `female` (transcribed from the forms of one person of that sex and checked against the standard adult interval of that sex — not lent to the other), or `unreviewed` (the corridor could not be checked against a form or a standard interval — lent to nobody until it is; the word is explicit so that the count can only shrink). A marker with `ref_by_sex` holds both and declares nothing here. Every marker with a corridor declares it: absence was how the question used to be spelled, and the suite refuses absence.
_meta.ref_age: Whether the corridor depends on age: `any` (one adult interval), `banded` (laboratories band this analyte by age and the band of the transcribed corridor was not recorded — lent to nobody, the reason is printed), or {min, max} in years (lent inside the band only; an unknown age is not a reason to guess). Declared by every marker with a corridor, for the same reason as ref_sex.
_meta.applies_to_sex: A test that exists for one sex only (PSA): not a corridor of that sex but a marker that does not apply to the other. For a profile of the other sex the value is shown and no corridor is — and the reason says the test, not the interval, is what does not apply. Implies ref_sex of the same sex.
_meta.method: The assay a series belongs to, for an element that laboratories measure two ways: `icp` (elemental analysis, ICP / ICP-MS, mass per litre) or `biochemistry` (clinical chemistry, molar). A series belongs to a method, not to a substance: a unit conversion is legitimate within a method and not across methods, so the ICP row of such an element accepts no molar unit and the two rows are separate keys. Declared, not inferred — `src/tools/check_method_mixing.py` reads it and refuses an element that mixes.

baso_abs.convert_note: 10³ per microlitre IS 10⁹ per litre — a factor of exactly 1, not a conversion. The US spellings (K/uL, K/µL) and the caret form (10^9/L) name the same quantity as the canonical 10*9/L; refusing them refuses the panel, not the unit.

calcium_blood.convert_note: Canonical here is mg/L; 1 mg/dL = 10 mg/L. No molar or equivalent unit is accepted on purpose: mmol/L and mEq/L are what the clinical-chemistry method prints, and that series is `calcium_total`. Until 12.09.2026 a ×40.08 entry here turned a biochemistry number into an ICP point.
calcium_blood.method_note: Elemental analysis (ICP / ICP-MS): the form prints the element with its symbol, in mg/L. Biochemical total calcium in mmol/L is a SEPARATE marker, `calcium_total`: the two methods disagree beyond rounding (more than ten per cent on the same sample has been seen), and putting them in one series would present a change of method as a trend. A unit conversion is legitimate within a method and not across methods — so this row's unit gate is mass-per-litre only, and a row in mmol/L is refused here rather than converted.

calcium_total.convert_note: Canonical here is mmol/L. Calcium A = 40.08 g/mol: 1 mg/dL = 10/40.08 = 0.2495 mmol/L, 1 mg/L = 0.02495 mmol/L; divalent, so 1 mEq/L = 0.5 mmol/L. The elemental (ICP) row `calcium_blood` keeps mg/L as its canonical unit on purpose — the two rows are different assays, not different units.
calcium_total.method_note: Total serum calcium by the biochemical method, in mmol/L. Kept apart from `calcium_blood` (elemental analysis, ICP, mg/L) for the reason `testosterone` is kept apart from `testosterone_immuno`: the same substance, two methods, numbers that disagree beyond rounding — more than ten per cent on the same sample has been seen. A series belongs to a method, not to a substance. The symbol in parentheses is a laboratory's typography, not a method, and since 12.09.2026 it is not excluded here. Today the parser hands a row to the longest matching name first, so a row that prints the symbol AND a molar unit reaches the ICP key, is refused by its unit gate, and is dropped rather than misfiled; it lands here the day the parser falls through on a refused unit.

cholesterol_total.convert_note: Cholesterol M = 386.65 g/mol; 1 mg/dL = 10/386.65 = 0.02586 mmol/L. The same constant applies to the LDL and HDL fractions — they are cholesterol, measured in a fraction.

copper.method_note: Elemental analysis (ICP / ICP-MS), reported in ug/L. Serum copper by the biochemical (colorimetric) method, in umol/L, is a SEPARATE marker, `copper_total`. magnesium_total.method_note: Serum magnesium by the biochemical method. t3_free.convert_note: Free triiodothyronine M = 650.98 g/mol; 1 pg/mL = 1 ng/L = 1.5362 pmol/L. Note that pg/mL belongs to free T3 and ng/dL to total T3 — the same number under the wrong one is off by a factor of ten, so the two markers keep separate tables.
t3_free.units_note: pg/mL → pmol/L: T3 is C15H12I3NO4, M = 650.98 g/mol; 1 pg/mL = 1 ng/L = 1e-9/650.98 mol/L = 1.536 pmol/L

t3_total.convert_note: Total triiodothyronine M = 650.98 g/mol; 1 ng/dL = 0.01536 nmol/L. Total T3 is reported in ng/dL and free T3 in pg/mL — the same number under the wrong unit is off by an order of magnitude, so the two keep separate tables.

t4_free.convert_note: Free thyroxine M = 776.87 g/mol; 1 ng/dL = 10/776.87 = 12.87 pmol/L. The US form is the commoner one on an American report, and free T4 arrives in it from every large reference lab.
t4_free.units_note: ng/dL → pmol/L: T4 is C15H11I4NO4, M = 776.87 g/mol; 1 ng/dL = 10 ng/L = 10e-9/776.87 mol/L = 12.872 pmol/L

testosterone.convert_note: Testosterone M = 288.42 g/mol; 1 ng/dL = 10/288.42 = 0.03467 nmol/L, 1 ng/mL = 3.467 nmol/L. The two spellings differ by a factor of 100.
testosterone.ref_sex_source: standard adult venous reference intervals, sex-specific; the male range is the historical default kept unchanged. A range printed on the person's own lab form always wins over this — this is used only when the value carries no form range.

tibc.convert_note: TIBC is expressed as the iron it can bind, so it converts on iron's molar mass, M = 55.845 g/mol: 1 µg/dL = 10/55.845 = 0.1791 µmol/L. Both spellings of micro are accepted because a report may carry either.
tibc.units_note: ug/dL → umol/L: TIBC is expressed as iron, M(Fe) = 55.845 g/mol; 1 µg/dL = 10 µg/L = 10e-6/55.845 mol/L = 0.17907 µmol/L

triglycerides.convert_note: Triolein M = 885.4 g/mol; 1 mg/dL = 10/885.4 = 0.01129 mmol/L. Note this is NOT the cholesterol constant — a common substitution, and it overstates triglycerides by a factor of 2.3.

tsh.convert_note: 1 µIU/mL = 1 mIU/L exactly. Both spellings are in wide use on forms and in reference ranges, and neither is a conversion.

urea.convert_note: Urea M = 60.06 g/mol; 1 mg/dL = 10/60.06 = 0.1665 mmol/L. BUN counts nitrogen only (2 × 14.007 = 28.01), so 1 mg/dL BUN = 10/28.01 = 0.357 mmol/L of urea — more than twice as much. Which one a lab reports is not visible in the number.

uric_acid.convert_note: Uric acid M = 168.11 g/mol; 1 mg/dL = 10000/168.11 = 59.48 µmol/L.
uric_acid.ref_sex_source: standard adult venous reference intervals, sex-specific; the male range is the historical default kept unchanged. A range printed on the person's own lab form always wins over this — this is used only when the value carries no form range.

vitamin_d.convert_note: 25-OH-vitamin D3 M = 400.6 g/mol; 1 nmol/L = 400.6/1000 = 0.4006 ng/mL. The parser's own `units` map rounds this to 0.4; typed input uses the full constant, and the difference at 75 nmol/L is 0.04 ng/mL.

wbc.convert_note: 10³ per microlitre IS 10⁹ per litre — a factor of exactly 1, not a conversion. The US spellings (K/uL, K/µL) and the caret form (10^9/L) name the same quantity as the canonical 10*9/L; refusing them refuses the panel, not the unit.

zinc.convert_note: A decimal prefix, not a molar conversion: 1 µg/dL = 10 µg/L exactly, because a decilitre is a tenth of a litre. Nothing here depends on a molar mass, and the factor cannot drift.
zinc.units_note: ug/dL → ug/L: a power of ten, 1 dL = 0.1 L
zinc.method_note: Elemental analysis (ICP), reported in ug/L. Serum zinc by the biochemical method, in umol/L, is a SEPARATE marker (`zinc_total`) for the same reason magnesium is: the two methods measure different fractions and share no corridor. This row's unit gate is mass-per-volume only — a row in umol/L is refused here rather than converted. ug/dL stays: it is a decimal prefix of the same quantity, and it is what a US panel prints.

zinc_total.convert_note: Canonical here is umol/L. Zinc A = 65.38 g/mol: 1 ug/L = 0.015296 umol/L.
zinc_total.method_note: Serum zinc by the biochemical method. Entered on 08.09.2026 together with `magnesium_total` and `calcium_total`: the third of one order of biochemical minerals, which the elemental series had been absorbing. The symbol in parentheses is a laboratory's typography, not a method, and since 12.09.2026 it is not excluded here. Today the parser hands a row to the longest matching name first, so a row that prints the symbol AND a molar unit reaches the ICP key, is refused by its unit gate, and is dropped rather than misfiled; it lands here the day the parser falls through on a refused unit.

copper_total.convert_note: Canonical here is umol/L. Copper A = 63.546 g/mol: 1 ug/dL = 10/63.546 = 0.1574 umol/L, 1 ug/L = 0.01574 umol/L. The elemental (ICP) row `copper` keeps ug/L on purpose — different assays, not different units.
copper_total.ref_sex_source: standard adult serum copper interval, sex-specific: 70-140 ug/dL for men and 80-155 ug/dL for women (Tietz), converted at A = 63.546 (x 0.1574). The male range is the default. A range printed on the person's own lab form always wins over this — it is used only when the value carries no form range.
copper_total.method_note: Serum copper by the biochemical (colorimetric) method, in umol/L. Entered on 12.09.2026 when the rule «a series belongs to a method, not to a substance» was applied to every element: the ICP row `copper` had been absorbing biochemistry rows by multiplying them by the atomic weight. The corridor is the standard adult interval, not one read off a form — a form range wins over it.
